positioning.statement: For Salesforce Solution Engineers, Technical Architects, Admins, Trailblazers, Partners, FDEs, Professional Services, Customer Success, and Account teams, MeshMesh is the Headless 360 orchestration platform that plans and executes end-to-end Salesforce work from plain-language intent, because it pairs deep validated knowledge of 40+ Salesforce products with a three-context intelligence model that compounds with every run and stops only when outcomes are verified.
positioning.primary_benefit: Collapses Salesforce setup and operations from months to minutes (~90% of time returned to the user).
positioning.differentiator: Salesforce-first knowledge + autonomous end-to-end execution (API and browser) + a learning flywheel that compounds.
positioning.audience: Solution Engineers, Technical Architects, Admins, Trailblazers, Partners, FDEs, Professional Services, Customer Success, Account Managers
ISVs, DET/DEX teams, internal tools & acquisitions, Salesforce customers
GovTech / highly regulated organizations; software-development companies
positioning.is_not: an IDE extension; a dev tool; a coding assistant; prompt-to-generate; an LLM wrapper; a replacement for Agentforce

strategic_context.vision: We make the complex, Salesforce simple.
strategic_context.definition: Maestro is Salesforce's new AI-native, agent-driven initiative to make using and implementing any Salesforce product simple.
strategic_context.meshmesh_role: MeshMesh is part of Maestro — the engine proving it works, today.
strategic_context.approved_line: Maestro is the vision. MeshMesh is the engine proving it works, today.
strategic_context.rule: Lead with Maestro for strategic/executive pieces; lead with MeshMesh when it's about the product doing the work.
Never conflate the Maestro value motion (Diagnose → Fix → Innovate) with the MeshMesh task flow (Define → Approve → Execute).

core_message.roof: MeshMesh collapses Salesforce setup from months to minutes. You define the outcome, approve the plan, and MeshMesh executes it end-to-end — and gets better with every run.

pillar.name: Salesforce-first, not code-first
pillar.proof: 40+ products; 387+ features; multi-org deploy + UAT; browser-beyond-the-API

pillar.name: Built for business users, plain language
Compounding intelligence
pillar.proof: Three-Context Model; intelligence flywheel; tenant-isolated learning

voice_attributes.rule: Address the reader in second person ("you", "your").
Lead with an outcome or a number, never a descriptive adjective.
Write metrics as numerals with a unit or multiplier (90%, 11x, 40+, 45 min).
Use active voice in all headlines and CTAs.
One value claim per sentence; no stacked superlatives.
Keep sentences short — aim for about 10 words; headlines shorter. One idea per sentence. Less is more. May be broken when clarity genuinely demands.
Use zero words from the forbidden list.
Use concrete verbs (plan, build, configure, deploy, test, document); not "handles/empowers/unlocks".
Pair any "autonomous" claim with the human approval gate.
In long-form, every statistic carries its source or qualifier.
Keep it sparse: cut every word the sentence still reads without.
Plain English at a high-school reading level; no clauses within clauses.
No corporate jargon or flowery/ornamental words.
Sound human, not generated: use zero phrases from the llm_tells list.
CTAs begin with a verb ("See the demo", "Start a plan"); never "Learn more" alone.

tone.mode: Confident, punchy; outcome-led headline with a number in the first line.
Encouraging, lightly celebratory; warm second-person guidance; at most one exclamation point; no hype words.
Neutral and factual; present-progressive title in progress ("Retrieving sales records…"), past-tense summary on completion ("19 sales records retrieved"); no technical jargon shown to business users.
Empathetic and solution-first; acknowledge, then give the next step; never blame the user; never expose stack traces.
Sober, precise, evidence-backed; cite frameworks; qualify every claim; no absolutes.
ROI-forward; lead with 11x ROI / hours saved; keep every number's qualifier.

translation_principle.rule: In business-user surfaces, describe the business result, never the technical action.
translation_principle.forbidden_surface_content: API names, HTTP verbs, endpoints, object API names, JSON payloads, stack traces

lexicon.note: "Salesforce sandbox" and "sandbox syncing" ARE correct — they name a Salesforce org type / capability. Only MeshMesh's own runtime must not be called a "sandbox".

forbidden_list.hype: game-changing, game-changer, revolutionary, supercharge, seamlessly, seamless, leverage, utilize, robust, paradigm, synergy, cutting-edge, bleeding-edge, disruptive, best-in-class, world-class, next-gen, next-generation, turnkey, frictionless, effortless, magic, magical, unparalleled, state-of-the-art, one-stop shop
forbidden_list.overclaim: 100% secure, unhackable, fully autonomous (unqualified), zero risk, guaranteed, always/never as reliability claims, set-and-forget
forbidden_list.llm_tells: delve, delve into, dive in, let's dive in, unlock, unlock the power of, elevate, elevate your, empower, empowering, harness, harness the power, navigate the complexities, in today's fast-paced world, in the ever-evolving landscape, it's important to note, it's worth noting, when it comes to, that's where X comes in, look no further, rest assured, whether you're X or Y, not only... but also, at the end of the day, the world of, the realm of, tapestry, testament to, boasts, designed to (as filler), in conclusion, first and foremost, a myriad of, plethora
forbidden_list.note: "Game-Changer" is permitted ONLY as the internal pilot time-savings tier label in validation tables, never as a marketing adjective.

competitor_rules.rule: Name competitors only for factual contrast: "Cursor, Claude Code, and Copilot know code, not Salesforce."
Never disparage a named competitor beyond the supported contrast.
Agentforce is a partner concept, not a rival: "MeshMesh doesn't replace Agentforce — it builds Agentforce… and beyond." Never position against Agentforce.
competitor_rules.approved_comparison_set: Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Agentforce Vibes, Traditional SI

formatting_rules.numbers: Use numerals for all metrics (40+, 387+, 90%, 3,500+, 100,000+, 45 min).
formatting_rules.ranges: En dash, no spaces: 9–12 months, 120–160 hours, $18–24K.
formatting_rules.distinct_claims: Keep separate: 11x ROI and 11.4x fewer steps (Jul 2026). Never merge or swap.
formatting_rules.capitalization: Sentence case for headings and UI labels. Capitalize proper nouns and MeshMesh terms (Headless 360, Three-Context Model). Do not capitalize "the plan", "the agent", "an outcome".
formatting_rules.punctuation: Oxford comma always. Em dash (—) for asides. En dash (–) for ranges. Avoid exclamation points (onboarding may use one). No semicolons in headlines.
formatting_rules.product_names: Spell out a Salesforce product on first use; acronym (MCE, MCA, FSC) after. Never invent a product name.

stat.value: 120–160 hrs manual (~$18–24K) delivered in 8–12 hrs guidance; 10–13x compression

hard_constraints.constraint: Never imply MeshMesh changes production without explicit human approval; planning and execution are separated by an approval gate.
Never imply cross-tenant data sharing; only business-stripped learnings return to the shared knowledge base.
Never use a proof-point number without its qualifier when the format allows one.
Never target excluded segments (GovTech/regulated, software-dev companies) in copy.
Keep internal per-use-case dollar/hour figures out of public-facing copy unless cleared.
